body: **visual-visibility ↔ screen-reader-support**: the listed set is bounded by the tree's exclusions (display none, visibility hidden, inert; a select's option excepted) (a11y-plan/visual-design-verification fct-lq4s5uty), and the read takes each listed node from the snapshot model that consumes that tree, with no second role or name mapping (a11y-plan fct-uz4kdss3); a node absent from the snapshot is never listed.

**visual-visibility ↔ the scope's shared refusal path**: the covered and off-screen causes come from action_point's one hit-test path, so inert pass-through, visibility hidden or collapse, a non-invertible transform, pointer-events none and an open list over a target (a11y-plan/visual-design-verification fct-pvwedula) (a11y-plan/visual-design-verification fct-zjxhbn6w) (a11y-plan/visual-design-verification fct-3g2s6aqs) (a11y-plan/visual-design-verification fct-h2b6iawo) each read the same in the list as in a real call, after the disabled check that the snapshot's `enabled` keys (a11y-plan fct-2hrkecxm).

**visual-contrast (lint) ↔ screen-reader-support (select as owner)**: the owner of an option or a list row is found by the select (closed_select_of, select_list_bounds) and never the role (a11y-plan/visual-design-verification fct-zlp57bv7), so CRUD's role="option" rows, not focusable and served by no select (a11y-plan fct-utkipxkl), are not listed as owner-served select rows, while a multiple select's rows read their own client rects (a11y-plan fct-uo5zb3r6).

**visual-contrast (lint) ↔ the new read's carriers**: like the lint verb on every carrier, recorded (a11y-plan/visual-design-verification fct-67ycdssr), the new read's written form holds ids, verb names and closed cause words only, never a node's value (a11y-plan fct-2hrkecxm).

body_fields.why: The owner-served nodes the read lists include a select's options, and their off-screen and covered causes must read the bounds the snapshot gives a closed select's options and an open list's rows.
body_fields.quote: a closed select's options under it, each with its select's client rect as its `bounds`; a select whose list is open is no closed select, `closed_select_of` answering `None` for it, and the snapshot's builder reads `select_list_bounds(node)` before the client rect, so an open row's `bounds` is its painted row's in the snapshot and the diff

body_fields.why: Whether an owner-served option can take a click now hangs on its select's open state, which lives in the tree's engine-state reading, and the read's verbs and causes for it must agree with that state.
body_fields.quote: A single select's tree node takes `expanded` from a closed bool of engine state, reading no `aria-expanded`, its focus staying on the select while the list is open

A single select reads `ComboBox` and writes `expanded` from its list's open state, reading no `aria-expanded`, and an author's `open` or `aria-expanded` on it steers nothing; the tree's focus stays on the select and its chosen option reads `selected`; the highlighted row is in no snapshot and no tree; the snapshot holds no `expanded` key, an open list's row reading its own `bounds` in the list

body_fields.why: The read lists from the snapshot and graph, so it must state no highlighted row of an open list, keeping this stated limit.
body_fields.quote: An open list's highlighted row is in no snapshot and no tree, a stated limit

body_fields.why: A multiple select's owner-served rows must take their off-screen and covered causes from their own client rects, in both layout modes.

A `multiple` select carries `set_multiselectable` in the tree and its rows read their own client rects in the snapshot

body_fields.why: The stable id the read lists per node must be the element's `author_id`, the same key the folded actionable-key reading reports as author key or positional path.
body_fields.quote: In a Dioxus document every element node carries its stable element id as AccessKit `author_id`, and no `TextRun`, document-root or `Window` node carries one
In a Dioxus document every element node carries its stable element id as AccessKit `author_id`, no `TextRun`, document-root or `Window` node one

body_fields.why: The read's nodes must be graph nodes that are snapshot nodes, its served ids must keep the reserved `///` form unused, and its read must change nothing and hold no typed text, as `stand_graph` asserts of the graph.
body_fields.quote: `stand_graph` asserts in both layout modes that every graph node is a snapshot node, that no served id holds the reserved separator `///` (the reserved `{owner}///{key}` form, spelled by `virtual_node_id`, which the walk never calls), and that a graph read changes nothing and holds no typed text

body_fields.why: The read's disabled cause must match the call's own refusal rule exactly, on the same reading and in the same order, its stand targets refused while not enabled.
body_fields.quote: `Session::run` refuses a `click` or a `type` as `disabled` when the snapshot node's `enabled` is `Some(false)`, the first of its three screen-level checks, with nothing dispatched and the ids reading `focused` and the tree's focus as they were before the call; on the stand `crud-delete` and `flight-return-date` are refused while they read not enabled and acted on once they read enabled, in both layout modes

a password input reads the fixed marker `MASKED_VALUE` where it holds text and `""` where it holds none

an element shot, addressed by stable id and refused as every id-addressed call is, is the node's bounds rounded outward and cropped to the part that can be seen — and a shot changes nothing: no focus moves, `has_changes` stays false and the next diff is empty, in both layout modes

its text form, parts, diff, MCP results, node-key help and `screenshot` read that model and nothing else, and the read-only UI graph (`DioxusDocument::graph`) holds one node per snapshot node, names and closed words only — never a second role or name mapping.

body_fields.why: The read's actionable set takes `clickable` as the snapshot gives it, from the walk's current listeners on no disabled form control, with no second role mapping.
body_fields.quote: `NodeState.clickable` is a `bool` after `focused`, true where the vdom walk's current listeners hold `click` and the element is no disabled form control (`ElementData::is_disabled`), read from the one snapshot model and the walk with no second role mapping

body_fields.why: The listed node must be the graph's node with its owner and handlers, and the read's answer must carry ids and closed words only, never a value.
body_fields.quote: a `UiGraph` holding one `GraphNode` per snapshot node in pre-order — its id, its `owner` (for an option or an optgroup, the stable id of its select), its component, its handlers with their declared writes, and the states it reads — and per registered state its declared writes, the writes a run confirmed or flagged (`undeclared`, `unconfirmed`) and its reading components; the answer carries ids, component names, state names, handler event names, closed flag words and booleans only, never a value

body_fields.why: An option's open-list state is not a snapshot reading, so the read must take it elsewhere or bring a new field to the founder, which moves the fourteen `NODE_FIELDS`.
body_fields.quote: No `expanded` node key exists: `NodeState` holds no such field and `NODE_FIELDS` reads fourteen, so a list's open state reaches the tree and not the snapshot

body_fields.why: The actionable set the read lists and the actionable-key fold the scope names are ruled by this rule and its check, with no second role mapping.
body_fields.quote: The actionable-key rule: every element an agent can act on — focusable, or carrying an interactive role, or carrying an event listener — reads an author key, so its `author_id` is that key and holds under any edit of the code around it (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-06); under dioxus-native-dom's `accessibility` feature `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` is the check — it reads focusability from `Node::is_focussable()`, the role from the tree `accessibility_tree` returns (a closed interactive list, so a disabled control is still held) and the listener mark `data-dioxus-id` (so a hidden control is still held, and so is an element whose listener a re-render removed, its mark still standing, so the check over-includes, conservative, while a `mounted` listener writes none — read, not run), with no second role mapping, and returns each actionable element whose id is a positional path, with its tag, its role and the remedy

`DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` is the check, with no second role mapping, and returns nothing on every stand task; the snapshot field `clickable` says an element reacts to a click, read from the vdom walk's current listeners and not the listener mark; the listener mark over-includes an element whose listener was removed (conservative).

body_fields.why: The read must take listeners from the walk, which reads them exactly, not from the mark, which over-reports; whether the actionable-key check's rule serves the read too is this fork.
body_fields.quote: The bridge's listener attributes over-report: a listener removed on a re-render leaves its event attribute and the `data-dioxus-id` mark standing while a click no longer acts, `remove_event_listener` lowering the per-kind count alone, and a `mounted` listener writes none; the vdom walk's dynamic attributes (`VNode.dynamic_attrs`, `VNode::mounted_dynamic_attribute`, public dioxus-core 0.7.10 API) read each element's current listeners exactly, `mounted` included, and the bridge's vdom walk yields them per element (`element_listeners`), the reading `NodeState.clickable` and the graph's handlers take, so neither over-reports as the mark does

body:
Builds one read-only driver read of the current screen's actionable nodes (v030-06, "What can I do here"): for each node an agent can act on, its stable id, its owner where its handler sits on another element, the verbs it takes, and per verb whether a call would be accepted now or the one refusal cause it would return (disabled, covered, off-screen).
The node model is the UI graph's agent-visible node (a GraphNode, one per snapshot node) with an optional owner element, so a select's handler serves its options and groups; nothing is keyed on a DOM NodeId.
The per-node verbs are read from the schema's verb table (VERBS, VerbSpec) with no closed list of verb names in the code; the table may need to say more, and that change, the carrier and the answer's shape are the founder's forks.
Its refusal causes come from the one shared path the executor uses (action_point: disabled, then off-screen, then covered), so they agree with a real call by construction; it runs no step, dispatches nothing and changes nothing, like snapshot, lint and graph.
If it fits, it folds in the actionable-key check (residual L12): each listed node says whether its id is an author key or a positional path; proven on the stand in both layout modes, with a minimal fixture for a covered, an off-screen and an owner-served target.

body_fields.what: the verb table VERBS and the new read's verb entry
VerbSpec, the per-verb statement of name, level, help, arguments and result fields
action_point, the shared refusal path (disabled, off-screen, covered)

body: The snapshot model the read consumes: role, name and focus from the accessibility tree, enabled from the presence of disabled, clickable from the vdom walk's current click listeners on an element that is no disabled form control, and each node's author_id; the read takes these from the model and adds no second role or name mapping.

The read-only UI graph (DioxusDocument::graph): one node per snapshot node, names and closed words only; the listed node is that graph node with an optional owner, and the new read must hold to names and closed words with no second role or name mapping.

The actionable-key rule and its check DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable: an actionable element is focusable, carries an interactive role or an event listener, and reads an author key; the check returns nothing on every stand task and uses no second role mapping; the listener mark over-includes an element whose listener was removed, while clickable reads current listeners.

Stable element ids as AccessKit author_id on every element node of a Dioxus document (no TextRun, document-root or Window node one): the id the read lists per node, and the author-key versus positional-path distinction the actionable-key check would report.
The disabled refusal: the driver refuses a click or a type as disabled where the snapshot's enabled reads Some(false), nothing dispatched; the read's disabled cause must match that rule exactly.

Disabled-ness keyed one way, by presence of the disabled attribute on a button, input, select or textarea (so disabled="false" still counts), and a falsy Dioxus value of a bridge boolean attribute removing the attribute; the read's disabled cause follows the same keying.
The focusability rule (tabindex, the natively focusable elements, inert and disabled form controls excluded), which decides the focusable part of the actionable set the read lists.

Visibility and hit-testing: display none, visibility hidden and inert exclude a node and its descendants from the tree and the snapshot, a select's option excepted from display none; a hit passes through an inert element; this bounds which nodes can be listed and what covered means.

Select as owner of sub-targets: an option of a closed single select takes no click, a click on a row of an open list chooses it, a disabled row changing nothing and a group header choosing nothing; a multiple select's rows read their own client rects; an optgroup reads Role::Group; an open list's row reads its own bounds and the highlighted row is in no snapshot; the owner-served node and its verbs and causes must agree with these.

The stand's CRUD list: person rows are options of a listbox by role, not focusable, the list crud-list the focus; how its rows are listed (own node or served by an owner) must agree with what a click on a row does.
Password and file input values read as the fixed MASKED_VALUE; the read carries ids, verb names and cause words only, never a node's value or typed text.
Both layout modes: the read's stand proof and its minimal fixture (covered, off-screen and owner-served targets) are asserted in both layout modes, as every stand check of the snapshot and graph is.

The snapshot's text form, parts, diff, MCP results and node-key help read the snapshot model and nothing else; a new carrier of the read on the socket call, CLI, MCP and a kept check reads the same model.
The tree's change set and refresh (changed_nodes, take_changed_nodes): a read that runs no step must not drain or depend on the changed set; a check reading has_changes() drains first.

the roles and names a check expects are stated once in the shared module's tables, never a second role or name mapping

body: Colour contrast (Harness::text_contrast, stand_contrast's tables, the lint's contrast reading, the select list's colour constants): the read names no colour and measures no ratio.

ARIA state attribute mapping (aria-selected, aria-pressed, aria-checked, aria-invalid to selected, toggled, invalid) and the merged states aria-expanded, aria-disabled, aria-level: the read lists verbs and refusal causes, not these states.
Accessible name and description computation (aria-label, aria-labelledby, label for, aria-describedby, aria-description): the read lists ids, not names.
The AccessKit platform adapter, accesskit_xplat, its windowed AT witness and residual res-llkgqygv: no adapter is built or read.
Per-key keyboard handling of range inputs, select typeahead and list keys, Enter and Space activation: the read dispatches no key.
Cells grid semantics (cells-grid, residual res-wvatzhpe) and the missing aria-activedescendant on the CRUD list: no role or cell semantics change.
Landmark roles inventory and the HTML-to-AccessKit role mapping, including the strong-native-semantics TODO: the read adds no role mapping.

body: **2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — made every Dioxus element node carry its stable id as AccessKit `author_id`, and no `TextRun`, document-root or `Window` node; dioxus-native-dom's `accessibility` feature gates its own tree override. The read's per-node id is this `author_id`, so the read sits behind the same gate.

**2026-10-06-headless-stand** — `disabled` was keyed two ways: state and click target read presence, focusability the parsed bool. It also first cleared a falsy Dioxus `disabled`. Trap: a `disabled` reading keyed on the value disagrees with `:disabled`. The read's `disabled` cause must use the presence keying, never the value.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — the snapshot takes role, name and focus from the tree `accessibility_tree` returns, with no second role or name mapping. This is the origin of the rule that the actionable read takes its node set from that model and adds no mapping of its own.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — founded the actionable-key rule (every element that is focusable, has an interactive role or carries a listener reads an author key) and its check `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable`, which takes the role from the tree. Trap: never satisfy the check by adding a `tabindex` or a role, because that moves the pinned Tab order; key the element instead. A folded key reading in the read must reuse this check.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** — the snapshot reads `enabled` from the presence of `disabled`, and a password reads `MASKED_VALUE`; a falsy Dioxus `hidden` no longer drops a node. The read's `disabled` cause rests on this `enabled`, and its answer must hold no value, masked or not.

**2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization** — a file input's value is masked like a password's, and `Snapshot::to_text` is one more reader of the model with no second mapping. A precedent: a new reader of the model adds no mapping and leaks no value.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — the shell takes the changed set (`take_changed_nodes`) on a poll and rebuilds the tree when that set is non-empty; `has_changes()` is true while it is non-empty. The read runs no step, so it must neither drain this set nor depend on it.

**2026-10-07-settle-detection** — a harness settle neither reads nor drains the changed set, and a freshly booted document's set is non-empty. So the read's no-change check must drain first and then read `has_changes()` false.

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — the driver's `disabled` cause was worded on the presence reading, and the schema defines no role or name set of its own. Rule: whatever detects `disabled` reads the snapshot's `enabled`, never the attribute value. The read's cause must keep to this rule.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — `escher-driver` names `accessibility` on dioxus-native-dom unconditionally, with no `[features]` table, and neither stand binary builds a platform adapter. The read in escher-driver reaches the graph, the snapshot and `unkeyed_actionable` through this edge and adds no adapter.

**2026-10-07-refusal-detection** — `Session::run` refuses `click` or `type` as `disabled` when `enabled` is `Some(false)`, the first of its three screen-level checks, with nothing dispatched. `crud-delete` and `flight-return-date` are the stand's cases. The read's `disabled` cause must match this check in order and in reading, through the shared refusal path.

**2026-10-10-snapshot-states** (the stand's listbox entry) — the CRUD list states `role="listbox"` and each row `role="option"`. The rows are not focusable, and the tree's focus is the list, never the option. The read must list CRUD's role-only options as their own nodes, not as select-owned rows.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — an MCP tool result reads the snapshot model and nothing else, over the crossing the founder ratified. A precedent for carrying the read's answer over MCP: it reads the model only, with no second mapping.

**2026-10-12-self-description** — a password typed over MCP reads `MASKED_VALUE`, and the typed sentinel appears 0 times. The node-key help and `differs` are readers that use closed words only. The read's no-value assertion can follow this sentinel-count form.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — `screenshot` reads only the model's bounds, rounded outward and cropped to what can be seen. A shot changes nothing: no focus moves, `has_changes` stays false and the next diff is empty, in both modes. This is the pattern for the read's no-mutation proof and a basis for an off-screen reading from bounds.

**2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness** — disabled-ness is keyed one way, by presence. The CRUD list takes `tabindex="0"` and becomes a focusable Tab stop while its rows stay unfocusable. Enter and Space activate a focused control. The read's focusable leg and its `disabled` cause follow this keying, and the read must list `crud-list` as its own focusable node.

**2026-10-14-quality-gates** — every `stand_*` file also runs three times in `stand-repeat` under the zero-failure budget. Trap: a new read check named `stand_*` joins `stand-repeat` by glob, which the binding says changes a11y-plan §9 and test-plan §10.

**2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep** — `unkeyed_actionable()` returns nothing on the non-lean tasks too (was 2 · 3 · 676). The elements that react to a click and state no role were counted: Circle Drawer 1, Cells 676. A folded key reading must re-assert empty on every task, and the read's set must agree with these counts.

**2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts** — the tree reads `aria-disabled` as disabled, but the snapshot's `enabled` never reads it. So the read must not name `disabled` for `aria-disabled` alone, matching the driver's refusal.

**2026-10-18-engine-debts** (§5, §6: `inert` and `disabled`) — focusability became: not inert (`Node::is_inert`) and no disabled form control (`ElementData::is_disabled`). A disabled form control stops the click walk; a disabled ancestor `div` does not. An inert subtree leaves the tree and the snapshot, and a hit passes through it. These bound the read's focusable leg, its exclusions and its `covered` cause (an inert element never covers). The founder ratified them at Epoch 2 close.

**2026-10-19-visual-lint** — the lint's `contrast` was first in process only, then (the gated part) the `lint` verb on every carrier, recorded, with findings written as ids, closed words and numbers only. That was the founder's F1 «Новая команда lint». It is the precedent that a new read verb on every carrier is a ratified boundary widening, which makes the read's verb and carrier the founder's fork.

**2026-10-20-select-by-id** — a click focuses a select but an option is not clicked. An option under a `select` stays in the tree under `display: none`; `hidden`, `inert` and `visibility: hidden` still exclude it. `select_interaction` and `stand_act_select` were introduced. These bound which owner-served options the read lists and why they are refused.

**2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts** — the driver's `snapshot` reads a screen over `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` in parts, on the founder's ratified paged answer. A precedent for the read's answer on Cells (676+ nodes) if it exceeds a carrier's budget.
**2026-10-24-a11y-re-read** — the `a11y` leg runs fourteen files on the founder's word; eight also run in `stand-repeat`. The read's new check stays out of the fourteen unless the plan is amended.

**2026-10-25-capability-statement** — `docs/capabilities.md` publishes the accessibility reach under `## Accessibility reach`, and its pin `.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py` reads none of those claims. Any change the read makes to the reach must be written into that document by hand.

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** (the flight booker's select) — `select#flight-type`, named `Flight type`, is the stand's select, with options `flight-type-one-way` and `flight-type-return`. A driver `click` on a flight-type option is refused `covered`. This is the stand's owner-served refusal case for the read.

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** (the served pages, the lint's option overlap, the scrollbar band) — `unkeyed_actionable` is empty on all six served tasks, the load page included; `load-done` is out of the tree while hidden. Right after a `scroll`, a click in the shown scrollbar band is a thumb drag that dispatches nothing until an `advance` passes the fade. The read's "acceptable now" answer must agree with that click.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (the load page's and Cells' rows) — the load page and Cells got Tab, keyboard and contrast rows (`LOAD_TAB_ORDER`, `CELLS_TAB_ORDER`), closing the served-pages gap. The read's stand proof must cover these two served tasks beside the lean four.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (`multiple` select tree and snapshot; `optgroup`) — a `multiple` select writes `set_multiselectable`, and its rows and groups read their own client rects while a closed select's options read the select's rect. `optgroup` became `Role::Group` named by `label`; a disabled group's rows read disabled through `option_disabled`. Together these give the owner-served rows' bounds and the read's `disabled` and off-screen causes for them.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (a `multiple` select's keys and row clicks; the driver on a `multiple` select) — `click_select_row` sits behind `handle_click`'s `option` arm; a disabled row changes nothing; an option of a closed single select, under a group too, is not clicked and stays refused `covered`. The driver's `type` on a `multiple` select focuses with no click, and the closed sets hold no verb, cause or field for it. The read's verbs for owner-served rows must agree with this.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (Cells by keyboard) — `cells-grid` carries `onkeydown` with no role, so the reacting elements on Cells are 677: 676 cells plus the grid. The read must give the grid a key verb but no `click`.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (the lint's closed-select overlap ended; a non-invertible transform) — `overlaps` finds a closed select's options through `closed_select_of` and never the role, so CRUD's `role="option"` rows are not taken as a select's. A non-invertible transform gives its subtree no hit. Owner-served detection follows the select, not the role, and `covered` and off-screen follow this hit rule.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the select list scope entity; what opens a list; a click, the pointer and focus on an open list) — `select_list` is an engine overlay that `hit_with_scrollbar` answers first. A row of an open list takes a click through `click_lands_on_row`; a group header chooses nothing; a disabled, inert or hidden select opens nothing. A closed single select's option is still refused `covered` (F9). The read's `click` and `covered` verdicts for owner-served nodes follow the list's open state.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (a single select's `expanded`; what the snapshot reads of an open list) — a single select writes `expanded` from engine state, not from `aria-expanded`. There is no `expanded` node key (`NODE_FIELDS`), the highlighted row is in no snapshot, and an open row's `bounds` come from `select_list_bounds`. The open state is not a snapshot reading, so the read must take it elsewhere or bring a new field to the founder.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (an open list against clips and `opacity`; the lint over an open list; a long list; the driver's `type` on any select) — a driver `click` on an element under an open list is refused `covered`. `Entry.in_select_box` finds rows through `closed_select_of` and `select_list_bounds`. The list's thumb takes no hit. `type` on any select focuses with no click and closes any list. The read's `covered` cause and verb table must agree with each of these.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the changed set where a list stands; the capability statement's named limits) — opening or closing a list marks the changed set, and a scroll or wheel with a list standing marks its select. The published limits now read: the fixup firing no `blur`, a single select's `size` unread, `aria-activedescendant` unread. The read must open or close no list, and the reach text it edits by hand keeps these limits.

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** — measured that an element reacts to a click (the link-2 reading) and that the listener mark `data-dioxus-id` over-reports after a re-render, so `unkeyed_actionable` over-includes, conservatively. `dioxus_runtime_probe` runs in the workspace `test` leg, outside the `a11y` and `stand-repeat` legs. The read's actionable set must use current listeners, not the mark (the measured fork), and its check follows the probe's leg placement.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (`NodeState.clickable`) — built `clickable` from the vdom walk's current `click` listeners on no disabled form control, with `NODE_FIELDS` 13 → 14. `stand_non_lean_tasks` gained a `CLICKABLE` table (Circle Drawer 1, Cells 676, the others 0) beside the mark's 677. `unkeyed_actionable` still reads the mark. The read's clickable leg and its stand counts rest on this.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the read-only UI graph reader `DioxusDocument::graph`) — `UiGraph` holds one `GraphNode` per snapshot node, with id, `owner` (an option's or optgroup's select), handlers and states; its answer is ids, names, closed flag words and booleans, never a value. It is gated behind `accessibility`. `stand_graph` asserts the graph is a subset of the snapshot, no `///`, no mutation and no typed text. The read's node model and its proof shape are this graph's.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (graph state registration and the bridge dispatch's write record) — `use_graph_state` and `DeclaredWrite` exist, and the bridge sets the registry's dispatch around `runtime.handle_event`. The read dispatches nothing, so it must never set or reach the registry's dispatch, and it leaves `graph.rs`'s recording unchanged.
partial — a driver read over the snapshot and UI graph, which a11y-plan models from the accessibility tree; no new UI surface, role, key binding or colour

- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (Accessibility tree output, the snapshot model) requires the snapshot to take role, name, focus and states from `accessibility_tree`, `enabled` from the `disabled` attribute and `clickable` from the vdom walk's current `click` listeners, and the read-only UI graph to hold one node per snapshot node; the actionable-node read must take its node set and its `disabled` reading from that model, never from a second role or name mapping.
- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (the graph reader, `DioxusDocument::graph`) requires each `GraphNode` to carry ids, its `owner` (an option's or optgroup's select), handler event names, closed flag words and booleans only, never a value; the per-node verbs and refusal causes the read adds must stay ids, verb names and closed cause words, no typed text or value (password `MASKED_VALUE` included).
- a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support (the actionable-key rule) requires every element an agent can act on (focusable, an interactive role or an event listener) to read an author key, `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` being the one check with no second role mapping; if the actionable-key check folds into this read, it must reuse that rule, not restate it.
- a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation (Focus order per layout) requires focusability to follow the engine's rule (not inert, no disabled form control, `tabindex`/native focusable elements, `disabled` by presence); the read's "focusable" leg of the actionable set must read `Node::is_focussable()`, not a list of its own.
- a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation (Focus restoration) states an option of a closed single select takes no click and a driver `click` on one is refused `covered`; the read must report that same cause for owner-served options, agreeing with the call.
- a11y-plan §6 Visual Design Verification (Visibility and hit-testing) requires nodes under `display: none`, `visibility: hidden` or `inert` to be out of the tree and so out of the snapshot, and a hit to pass through an inert element; such nodes must not be listed as actionable, and whether the shared refusal path already reflects this is research's question.
- a11y-plan §9 CI Integration requires the `a11y` leg's fourteen files unchanged unless a chunk states otherwise; a new read check runs in the workspace test leg (as `stand_graph` and `dioxus_runtime_probe` do) unless the plan is amended.

- `stand_graph` asserts in both layout modes that every graph node is a snapshot node and that a graph read changes nothing and holds no typed text (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support); the same shape suits the actionable read's no-mutation, no-value assertions.
- `stand_act_select` and `select_interaction` already pin a driver `click` refused `covered` on a closed select's option (per a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation, Focus restoration); usable as the owner-served refusal case.
- The driver refuses `click`/`type` as `disabled` where the snapshot's `enabled` reads `Some(false)`, nothing dispatched (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support); the read's `disabled` cause sits on the same reading.
- Stated tables with their row counts asserted, in both layout modes (per a11y-plan §3 A11y Assertion Harness Contract); a per-task table of expected actionable nodes and causes follows that form.

- No second role, name or focusability mapping beside the tree, snapshot and `unkeyed_actionable` (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).
- No value or typed text in the read's answer, only ids, closed words and booleans (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support, the graph reader).

- a11y ↔ driver/security: the read's answer and the `command` span carry closed words and ids only, per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support's graph-reader rule beside doc:security-plan §Surfaces.
- a11y ↔ tests: a new stand check goes in the workspace test leg; joining the `a11y` leg or `stand-repeat` changes a11y-plan §9 CI Integration and test-plan §10.

- On every stand task, in both layout modes, each listed node is a snapshot/graph node and every `clickable` or focusable snapshot node is listed; no listed node is under `display: none`, `visibility: hidden` or `inert` (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support and §6 Visual Design Verification).
- A node whose snapshot `enabled` reads `Some(false)` lists cause `disabled`, and a closed single select's option lists `covered`, each matching the refusal an actual `click` returns (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support and §5 Keyboard Navigation).
- The read changes no snapshot, focus or tree, and its answer holds no typed or masked value (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).
- If the actionable-key check folds in, its unkeyed set equals `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable`'s, empty on every stand task (per a11y-plan §7 Screen Reader Support).

body_fields.why: the new read must run through Session::run after validate like every verb, with nothing public running a Command validate did not produce.

**Driver session (escher-driver):** a `Session` (one booted app) runs every call through `Session::run`, which validates first; nothing public runs a `Command` that did not come from `validate`; the command and refusal schema stated once as `'static` data — thirteen verbs, eight closed causes, no refusal holding what a call supplied; the `v3` wire, the command line, the MCP server and the `command` and `tool_call` spans carry it; no `NodeId` crosses, and nothing logs an id, a name or a value.

body:
Adds one read-only driver read, beside snapshot, lint and graph, that lists each actionable node on the current screen with its stable id, its owner where its handler sits on another element, its verbs, and per verb whether a call would be accepted now or the one refusal cause (disabled, covered, off-screen) the call would return.
The node model is the UI graph's GraphNode with an optional owner (a select serving its options and groups), never keyed on a DOM NodeId; the verbs are read from the schema's verb table VERBS with no closed list of verb names in this code, which may need VerbSpec to say more (a contract change, the founder's fork).
The read and the executor decide a target's refusal through one shared path (today action_point in execute.rs: disabled, then off-screen, then covered), so the list agrees with a real call by construction.
The actionable-key check (residual L12) may fold in, each listed node saying whether its id is an author key or a positional path, if P4 finds it fits.
Proven on the stand in both layout modes, with a minimal fixture where the stand lacks a covered, an off-screen or an owner-served case; no engine change is expected.

body: The driver session contract: one Session running every call through Session::run after validate, the command and refusal schema stated once as static data (its count of verbs and closed causes), no refusal holding what a call supplied, carried by the v3 wire, the command line, MCP and the command and tool_call spans.

The driver session boundary decision: ids, names, closed flag words and booleans may cross, never a NodeId; a new carrier or a new verb on every ratified carrier widens the boundary, which is the founder's fork.

The UI graph and snapshot of the Dioxus DOM bridge: DioxusDocument::graph (UiGraph of nodes), the snapshot read read-only with no NodeId, and the snapshot's clickable reading an element's own current click listener on no disabled form control.

Stable element ids in four tiers (author key, anchored path, component path, document path) and the reserved owner form spelled by virtual_node_id, which the node model's optional owner must stay open to.

The actionable-key rule: every element an agent can act on reads an author key, and unkeyed_actionable lists, read-only, each actionable element whose stable id holds a slash, with its remedy; its actionable set (focusable, interactive role, listener) bounds which nodes the read lists.

The refusal semantics the shared path must keep: the disabled reading through ElementData::is_disabled and option_disabled, seeing read through visible_region never from a hit, a hit stopping at clipping boxes and an open select list answered first, and an option of a closed single select staying refused covered.

The select tests the driver reads (closed_select_of, is_select via locate, is_masked_input) and the select model's options as the select's children in the snapshot: the owner-served case today is a select serving its options and groups.

Every driver answer written by hand in the crate-private json module, no serialization crate writing one, serde_json only reading MCP requests and kept checks, and no command's ending writing back what the caller typed.
The command span records verb and, refused, cause alone; no log or event carries the read's content, its size, an id, a name or a value.

The recording and replay of a kept check: answered calls kept owner-only in the launcher-named recording directory and replayed through Session::run; the two committed stand checks under tests/blitz-tests/checks are the one owner-only exception.

The escher-session command line over the six served stand tasks, answering one line of JSON with exit codes 0 accepted, 1 refused, 2 usage, 3 session error, and the MCP server named escher listing the driver's commands as tools.
The headless stand (seven_guis::stand: four lean tasks, Cells, the load page, pinned 800x600 Light viewport) on which the read is proven, in both layout modes.
The front page README.md's count of driver commands an MCP client gets as tools, read by the capability-statement pin, which a new read changes.
The engine-change rule: the engine's direct changes are ratified one by one and flagged upstreamable; any engine change this chunk finds it needs is the founder's fork, not taken here.
The read changes nothing: like Session::lint and the graph, it runs no step, dispatches nothing, moves no virtual clock time and waits on no load.

body: The browser app, its history store, document loader, URL suggester and about pages: the chunk reaches only the driver, the Dioxus bridge's reads and the stand.
The WPT runner, its outputs, bucketing and CI WPT workflows: nothing in the chunk runs or changes them.
JavaScript on Boa (blitz-vibey-script), its bootstrap, timers and module loader: the stand is Dioxus and the read touches no script.
Networking (blitz-net), outbound hosts, the user agent and resource loading: the read makes no fetch.
Painting, renderer backends, the password mask and screenshot rendering: the read paints nothing and takes no shot.
Fonts, CSS approximations, unsupported CSS features and Taffy layout internals: the chunk changes no style or layout behaviour.
Upstream sync bookkeeping and the merge surfaces of the ratified engine changes: the chunk merges nothing from upstream.
Nix packaging, cross-compilation, the publish-browser deployment and release versioning: no packaging or release change.
The shell loop, windowing, launch paths, hot reload and the accessibility adapter: the read runs headless through the driver session.
The example fixture forms (google and graphite pages) and the HTML fixture pages under examples/assets: the chunk's fixtures are stand fixtures.
Drag, virtual-node production, the canvas and two-target verbs: they stay in 0.4.0, the shapes only kept open.
Handler coverage (v030-07) and auto-exploration (v030-09): their own entries.

body: **2026-10-06-stable-element-ids** — stable element ids registered: `element_id` / `element_ids()` computed on demand, no `NodeId`, `ElementId`, `ScopeId` or pointer in an id. Why it matters: the read lists nodes by exactly these ids, the ids the per-node verbs resolve, and an author key versus a positional path is the grammar the actionable-key fold-in has to tell apart.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — snapshot model registered under `accessibility`. Each field is an existing reader's (`enabled` is the `disabled` presence), and no field holds a `NodeId`. Standing rule: the snapshot derives no role or name of its own, so it cannot disagree with the accessibility tree. Why it matters: this is the precedent for the read's "no second reading" rule (refusal causes from the engine's readers, not re-derived).

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** (actionable-key check) — registers `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable()` with its three readers (focusable, a closed interactive-role list, `data-dioxus-id`), its seven fields and `remedy()`, with no wire form; adds the anchored-path tier. Trap stated for later chunks: `UnkeyedActionable.node` is a process-local `NodeId`, so the first wire form of the check must not carry it. Why it matters: folding the check into this read is that first wire form.

**2026-10-07-driver-session** — the session socket is a founder-ratified boundary widening. Standing rule: the first request that carries an id, a name, a value, snapshot text or a diff is a new crossing question. Why it matters: this is where the "a new carrier or exit widens the boundary" rule starts, and the new read's answer must clear it.

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — builds the one `'static` table: `VERBS`, `VerbSpec`/`ArgSpec`/`FieldSpec`, `verb(name)`, `validate`, a closed `Cause` and a `Refusal` with no `String` field. Standing rule: a later entry adds its verbs to `VERBS`, never a second table. Why it matters: reading per-node verbs from the table with no closed list in code rests on this rule. Any field that says a verb's targets or refusals extends this shape, and that is a contract fork.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — `Session::run` is the one entry point. Nothing public runs a `Command` that did not come from `validate`, nothing resolved outlives a call, and nothing fields an `Outcome` (its `Debug` prints ids, names and values). Why it matters: the new read's `Command` and `Outcome` variants go through `run`, and the new `Outcome` must stay unlogged.

**2026-10-07-refusal-detection** — the executor detects the screen-level refusals. A `click` or `type` is refused in the fixed order `disabled` · `off-screen` · `covered` with nothing run. Resolution answers `stale`/`not-found` against the session's `SeenIds` record. Adds `visible_region` and the `scroll` verb, which applies none of the three checks. Standing rule: visibility is read from geometry, never from a hit. Why it matters: this is the shared refusal path (`action_point`) the read must reuse so its causes agree with a real call.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** — one hand-built `command` span per call to `Session::run` (no `#[instrument]`) with eight fields; a refused call records `verb` and `cause` only; arguments, `Outcome` and screen content are never fielded. Why it matters: the new read's span records `verb` alone (and `cause` when refused), with no field for its content or size.

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** (the socket carries a call and its answer) — the founder ratified the second widening: ids, names, masked values, snapshot text and diffs cross the socket with no `NodeId`, and the answer is bounded at 1,048,576 bytes. Standing rule: the next surface that carries them asks again. Why it matters: these are the carrier and bound the new read's answer crosses.

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** (nine verbs in two levels, the written forms, `command_line`) — adds `Level`, the session-level verbs and the hand-written `Outcome::to_json`/`Refusal::to_json`; no command ending writes back caller input; the usage line and argv reader read `VERBS`, with no second list. Why it matters: the new verb reaches the command line and its written form through these hand-written forms.

**2026-10-10-scrolling-box-bounds-and-hit** — a box's client rect no longer subtracts its own scroll offset, and the hit stops at the padding box of a box that clips by `overflow`. These are direct engine changes, and the founder's ruling set their reach. Why it matters: the off-screen and covered causes the read predicts depend on these two readers staying as ratified.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** (MCP crossing ratified) — `serve_mcp` with `tools/list` over `VERBS`; ratified boundary widening over the `mcp` role's stdio. Standing rule: the next surface that carries a call or a screen's content is a new crossing question. Why it matters: the new verb becomes an MCP tool on this ratified carrier.

- The read has to go through the driver session's single validated path. Architecture §Standard Contracts (Driver session) requires every call to run through `Session::run`, which validates first. Nothing public may run a `Command` that did not come from `validate`. The command and refusal schema is stated once as `'static` data: thirteen verbs in `VERBS` and eight closed causes, and no refusal holds anything a call supplied. A new verb or cause changes that count and that table, so it is the founder's contract fork.
- No `NodeId` may cross a boundary. Architecture §Established Decisions ([Driver session]) allows a session to carry only ids, names, closed flag words and booleans, and never a `NodeId`. The same section says a new carrier or exit widens the boundary. Answering this read on the socket `call`, the command line, MCP and a kept check is a boundary question for the founder.
- Answers are written by hand. Architecture §Standard Contracts (Driver session) requires every answer to be written in the crate-private `json` module. No serialization crate may write one: `serde_json` only reads MCP requests and kept checks. No command's ending may write back anything the caller typed.
- The node model comes from the UI graph and the snapshot, read-only. Architecture §Standard Contracts (Dioxus DOM bridge) requires `DioxusDocument::graph`, the snapshot and `element_id` to read the screen read-only, under `accessibility`, holding no `NodeId`. It reserves the fifth id form `{owner}///{key}`, spelled by `virtual_node_id`, which no walk writes. The snapshot's `clickable` reads an element's own current `click` listener and never a disabled form control.
- The `disabled` rules have one source each. Architecture §Standard Contracts (Nodes and widgets) requires `ElementData::is_disabled` to be the one disabled reading for a form control, and `option_disabled` the one rule for an option. Architecture §Established Decisions ([DOM semantics]) has focusability, the pointer and click gates, and Enter/Space activation all read that same one reading. A refusal cause in the list must come from these readers and must not re-derive them.
- What counts as visible and what counts as hit stay separate. Architecture §Standard Contracts (Scrolling, selection, tree) makes `visible_region` the read-only reader of what can be seen, and seeing is never read from a hit. A hit stops at the padding box of a box that paint clips, and an open select list answers first in `hit_with_scrollbar`. The off-screen and covered causes have to read these same readers.
- No engine change is expected. Architecture §Established Decisions (direct engine changes) records each engine change as a direct change for every document, with a merge surface owned by Upstream sync. The scope keeps the engine untouched, so any engine change that comes up is the founder's fork.

- Read-only verb precedent: `graph` takes no argument (an argument is refused `malformed` and nothing runs) and answers `Outcome::Graphed`. Its node ids feed the session's record of ids, and it is written by hand as `{"nodes":[…],"states":[…]}` with `owner` left out when absent (per architecture §Standard Contracts, Driver session, the UI graph verb). A new read can follow the same shape: no argument, a dedicated `Outcome`, and optional keys left out.
- Schema shape types: each `VerbSpec { name, level, help, args, fields }` is built from `ArgSpec`/`FieldSpec` and found only by an exact-name `verb(name)` lookup (per architecture §Standard Contracts, Driver session). Reading per-node verbs from the table, with no closed list in code, means reading from these types. Whether today's `VerbSpec` already states each verb's target applicability is research's question.
- Self-description and the capability pin read everything from the tables (`VERBS`, `NODE_FIELDS`, `CAUSES`, …), and `tools/list` answers the verbs of `VERBS` in order (per architecture §Standard Contracts, Driver session). The capability-statement test reads verb names from `VERBS` and the verb count from `docs/capabilities.md` and `README.md` (per architecture §Project Intent, Front page).
- The stable-id tiers (author key, anchored path, component path, document path) and `unkeyed_actionable`, which lists, read-only, each actionable element whose stable id holds a `/` (per architecture §Standard Contracts, Dioxus DOM bridge). This is the existing reading the actionable-key fold-in would reuse.

- No closed list of verb names or causes in the new read's code. The verb and cause set lives once in the `'static` schema (per architecture §Standard Contracts, Driver session).
- No logging of the read's content. Nothing may log an id, a name or a value (per architecture §Standard Contracts, Driver session). No log or event may carry the snapshot or its text, beyond a diff's three counts (per architecture §Standard Contracts, Dioxus DOM bridge).
- No engine-side refusal logic duplicated in the driver. One disabled reading and one visibility reader stand in the engine (per architecture §Standard Contracts, Nodes and widgets, and §Standard Contracts, Scrolling, selection, tree).

- arch ↔ security: the boundary rule (ids, closed words and booleans only, no `NodeId`) and the "a new carrier or exit widens the boundary" rule (architecture §Established Decisions, [Driver session]) bind to security's carrier review. The `command` span keeps `verb` and, when refused, `cause` alone.
- arch ↔ obs: the escher-driver spans are ungated and hand-built, with no `#[instrument]` (architecture §Conventions, Feature gating). No new span field may hold the read's content or size.
- arch ↔ tests: scenarios run in both layout modes, and tests first assert that the fixture produces the condition (architecture §Conventions, Tests). Stand checks share helpers through non-target modules under `tests/`. Recording and replay of a kept check go through `Session::run` (architecture §Standard Contracts, Driver session).
- arch ↔ docs: `docs/capabilities.md`, `README.md` and `.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py` pin the verb count (architecture §Project Intent, Front page).

- The new read's code lives in `packages/escher-driver`, and the graph and snapshot readers in `packages/dioxus-native-dom`. No new crate, no new dependency outside `[workspace.dependencies]`, and no engine change (per architecture §Existing Scopes and §Conventions, Manifests).
- The read's written form holds no `NodeId`, no value and nothing the caller typed. It is written by hand in the `json` module, with optional keys left out when absent (per architecture §Standard Contracts, Driver session).
- If a verb is added, `VERBS`, `tools/list`, the usage line, `help`, `docs/capabilities.md` and the capability pin all agree on the new count, and that change is recorded as a founder-ratified contract and boundary fork (per architecture §Standard Contracts, Driver session, and §Established Decisions, [Driver session]).
- Each listed refusal cause is one of the existing closed causes. It is decided through the same path the executor uses, so on the stand, in both layout modes, it matches the refusal an actual call returns (per architecture §Standard Contracts, Driver session, and §Conventions, Tests).

body:
Adds one read-only driver read of the current screen's actionable nodes (v030-06), dispatching nothing, like snapshot, lint and graph.
For each node it gives the stable id, the owner element where the handler sits on another element, the verbs it takes, and per verb whether a call is accepted now or the one refusal cause (disabled, off-screen, covered) the call would return.
The node model is the UI graph's GraphNode with an optional owner, so a select's handler serves its options and groups, and nothing is keyed on a DOM NodeId; verbs come from the schema's verb table VERBS with no closed list of verb names.
Refusal reasons come from the same path the executor uses (action_point: disabled, then off-screen, then covered), so they match a real call. The actionable-key check (author key vs positional path) folds in if it fits.
It is proven on the stand in both layout modes, with a minimal fixture where the stand lacks a covered, off-screen or owner-served case.

action_point, the shared refusal path

body: The cli surface's output rule: the driver's command line and its mcp role print only JSON on stdout, one line per command or newline-delimited JSON-RPC lines, with no colour or ESC byte and no terminal test; the exit status carries the class (0 accepted, 1 refused, 2 usage, 3 session error). The new read's answer must follow it.

The cli surface's graph read (the cli-graph subject) and the pending unpaged-graph subject: the new read is a sibling of graph and reads the same UI graph, so how graph's answer is shaped and paged on the command line applies to it.
The cli surface's component patterns for the driver's agent-read outputs, which cover the snapshot, lint and graph reads the new read sits beside.

Hit-testing as the depth strategy states it: a point outside a paint-clipping box (overflow, or contain including paint, root excepted) reaches none of its children, and an open select list's row is answered before the walk. This decides the covered cause the read reports through action_point, and why an owner-served select row is not clipped.

The open select list's rows as owner-served sub-targets: a select's handler serves its options and groups, and the rows are answered and scrolled by the select list itself (SelectListView). The read lists them under their select owner.

Into-view scrolling as the motion section states it: the driver's scroll is instant in every box and the viewport, and into view on an open select row moves only that list's scroll. This governs the off-screen cause and keeps the read from scrolling or moving anything.
The harness clock rule: click, type and press leave the VirtualClock where it was, and only advance moves it. The read dispatches nothing, so it must not move the clock or wait on settle.

The disabled state of a target, the first cause action_point checks, which the read reports per verb; the select list's DISABLED_TEXT row colour is how a disabled option is painted, not how it is detected.

The cursor rule, Pointer inside links and Text for text inputs, only as a sign of which elements a person sees as actionable; the actionable set itself comes from handlers, owner-served nodes and the unkeyed_actionable criteria.

The screenshot fonts-unavailable refusal and the system-fonts build feature: the stand proof in both layout modes depends on text measuring non-zero, otherwise off-screen and covered checks pass vacuously.

body: **2026-10-10-driver-cli** (the driver command line's output form) — set the `escher-session` form: one line of JSON on stdout per command keyed by the schema's own words, no colour, no ESC byte, no terminal test, exit status 0 accepted · 1 refused · 2 usage · 3 session error; the new read's answer line inherits this form unchanged and adds no exit status.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** (the `mcp` role's stdout) — the `mcp` role's stdout holds only newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 lines, a tool result's text the JSON line (screen text for `snapshot`), no ESC byte asserted on every reply by the shared `Speaker`; the new read's MCP tool result must take this form and pass through `Speaker`.

Builds one read-only driver read of the current screen's actionable nodes (v030-06): each node's stable id, its optional owner, its verbs read from the schema's verb table VERBS with no closed list of verb names, and per verb whether a call would be accepted now or the one refusal cause it would return.

Refusal causes come from the one path the executor uses (action_point: disabled, then off-screen, then covered), so the read agrees with a real call by construction.
It runs no step, dispatches nothing and changes nothing, like snapshot, lint and graph; the actionable-key check (residual L12) may fold in if it fits.
The verb-table change, the carrier (socket call, command line, MCP, kept check) and the answer's shape are founder forks; proven on the stand in both layout modes with minimal fixtures for covered, off-screen and owner-served targets.

The tool_call span over MCP: a new verb answered on the MCP server opens one tool_call span whose tool field is the verb table's word and whose ending is accepted, refused or error; no other field.
The escher-driver span census: the crate keeps its 2 info_span! sites and emits no event; the new read adds no span, event, log site, subscriber or env read.

The new answer (a new Outcome variant, beside Outcome::Graphed and Outcome::Linted) is written by Outcome::to_json alone as a command's answer, over MCP its JSON line, kept whole in a recorded check, and never logged, fielded or printed with Debug.

The answer carries stable ids, verb names and closed cause words (disabled, covered, off-screen) and booleans only, never a NodeId, page text or control value; the PII scrub of escher's sink and the content-named span field set apply to anything that does reach a span.

The recording module writes each answered call's arguments, accepted, the answer digest and the answer into the kept check at rest through the crate's json writer, never as a log line, field or print; replay reads with serde_json only.

The executor modules command, refusal, schema and execute install no subscriber, read no env var and no clock, and print nothing; a shared refusal path reused by the read keeps that.

body: **2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** (the cause names are the owed span field's domain) — made the driver's schema (`validate`, `VERBS`, `Refusal` with `Cause`) silent and set the rule that the span's cause field takes a `Cause::name` only, never a `Command`, `Call` or `ArgValue` with `Debug`, nor an argument by its schema name. This chunk edits `VERBS` / `VerbSpec` and returns per-verb causes, so it must keep using `Cause::name` words and keep the new outcome out of `Debug`.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** (the executor is silent) — `execute`, `Session::run` silent; `Outcome` joined the `Debug`-deriving types nothing prints, logs or fields, since an `Outcome` fielded with `Debug` would print an id, name or value. The new read's `Outcome` variant inherits this rule.

**2026-10-07-refusal-detection** (eight cause names returned) — the refusal detection (the `disabled` / `covered` / `off-screen` path now behind `action_point`) was built under the crate's silence constraint and all eight cause names became returned by code. The read's per-verb causes come from this one path and its closed words.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** (the driver's command span as built) — fixed the `command` span: INFO at `escher_driver`, eight fields recorded only where they apply, a never-fielded list (any argument, `Command`, `Call`, `ArgValue`, `Outcome`, `Refusal`, `Fault`); `stand_act_spans`' re-run children are the census exception. The new read verb must enter this span with `verb` alone (or `verb` + `cause`) and add no field.

**2026-10-09-founder-rulings** (the closed span's line ratified) — the closed-span line, a boundary widening, ratified by the founder; any new field or record class is again a founder's ruling. The read adds none, so it stays inside this ratified line.

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** (the session host writes the command span; the command line writes answers, not logs) — a hosted `call` runs through `Session::run` alone, one closed `command` span per call, and a call refused on the command line or in the client opens no span; a command's answer is one JSON line on stdout, never a log line. Standing rule: the next surface adds no span or log field holding what a call supplied or a screen reads. This binds the read on the socket's `call` and the command line, if the founder picks those carriers.

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** (typed text measured in a host's log) — `host_log` reads a hosted `type` sentinel, ids and names at 0 at `trace` under both builds. This is the needle reading the new read's `host_log` call extends.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** (the `tool_call` span, ratified) — added the `tool_call` span (`tool`, `ending` only, ratified by the founder as a new log field), with `command` its child by nesting, plus `mcp_log` and `stand_mcp_tools`' in-process recorder. The new read's MCP tool call must open one `tool_call` holding only these two closed words.

**2026-10-12-self-description** (`help` in the two spans' closed sets) — a verb joining the table joined both spans' closed sets with no field added, and `describe` was recorded silent. Self-description text is an answer on stdout, never a log line. This is the precedent for the new verb's `describe.rs` / help text.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** (`screenshot` in the spans' closed sets) — the pattern for adding a verb: the `command` line's word count, instance count and `tool_call` count all move, never-fielded gains the answer's content and size, and an empty crop is refused `off-screen`. The read moves the same counts (thirteen → fourteen, nine → ten instance verbs) and must never field its node list or its size.

**2026-10-15-cold-agent-test** (the cold-agent pipe log on the escher server) — the pipe counts the live child's `tool_call` / `command` lines in `server.log` and is a reader, not an emitter. A new verb reaches this reader through its `tool_call` line only.

**2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock** (eight causes) — `time-unavailable` was retired, leaving eight cause names (six returned by the executor). The read's per-verb refusal causes must be drawn from these eight.

**2026-10-18-engine-debts** (the PROVISIONAL batch ratified, one-virtual-clock) — the founder ratified the eight cause names, `covered` and `off-screen` among them. The read's cause words rest on this ratified set, and adding a new cause word would need a new ruling.

**2026-10-19-session-recording** (recording opens no span and logs nothing) — the recording module records every call with no span of its own. A call after the recording ended ends `tool_call` `error` with `tool` / `ending` alone. The new read recorded in a kept check goes through this path.

**2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay** (each kept answer at rest, the committed checks) — the answer is kept whole as `answer`, masked as on every carrier, and replay adds no span. The two committed Counter checks are read by `stand_replay` and the freshness check (ratified widening). Changing the verb table or the kept-check form must leave both replaying and free of typed text.

**2026-10-19-test-splits** (the log checks' shared fragment) — seven_guis' `tests/common/mod.rs` holds `Needles`, `stand_needles` and `recorded_needles` for `host_log` / `mcp_log`, and its assertion messages carry a kind and a count only. The read's needle tests extend this module, and their messages must stay needle-free.

**2026-10-19-visual-lint** (the gated part: the `lint` verb inside the command span, no field) — the founder's F2 «no new span field» with F1 a new verb: `Session::lint` reached inside the call's `command` span, opening none of its own, recording `verb` alone, with its findings and count never fielded. This is the direct no-field precedent for a read verb.

**2026-10-20-select-by-id** (the PROVISIONAL discharge) — the lint's «no new field» was dropped from PROVISIONAL on the founder's own word, so the no-new-field rule for read verbs is founder-ratified.

**2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts** (a part read's span and its silence) — a read records `verb` alone, its number, count and size never fielded. `host_log` / `mcp_log` drive one part read at `trace`, and `stand_act_spans` gained one call per mode. The read follows the same per-verb span and needle pattern.

**2026-10-24-stand-requirement-sweep** (the paged part and the recording clients read) — `stand_act_spans` went to 36 calls per mode, with ids and button text as needles, and `host_log` reads a recording session's clients at `trace`. This is a call count and needle set the new read's call extends.

**2026-10-25-capability-statement** (the statement restates the driver's spans) — `docs/capabilities.md` restates the emitter's reach, and its pin reads none of it, so any span-set change is made by hand. The kept check's at-rest list extends with each new answer type, which is a trap for this chunk's `docs/capabilities.md` edit.

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** (the cold-agent pipe's verdict fields) — counted verbs (`lint` · `screenshot` · `advance`) and their `capability-unused` reason, read from `server.log`'s accepted `tool_call` lines. A new verb is uncounted unless added here, and `tool_call` keeps two fields.

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** (the host-sink part read measured) — `host_log`'s fourth test runs `serve cells` at `trace` and counts the host's closed `command` span lines, with 0 id and 0 name needles. This is the hosted-read precedent the new read's host carriage follows.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the select list adds no log site or span) — `click` / `type` / `press` help and `covered`'s meaning are fixed `'static` text that reaches no field, kept outside the widening under the 2026-10-12 rule. `command` keeps its eight fields, and escher-driver keeps 2 `info_span!`. Any target, refusal or help text `VerbSpec` gains falls under this rule.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the harness contract takes the graph verb and its never-logged answer) — `graph` became the ninth instance verb under one `command` span. `Outcome::Graphed` is written by `to_json` alone, never logged or fielded, and `session_common` readers went to thirty-three. The new read follows as the next verb, and its `Outcome` gets the same never-logged clause and reader count.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the graph answer's carried set, ratified) — the `graph` answer's ids, names and closed words were added at rest to the Recording directory row and to the §8 boundary widening. The confirm that the proposals lie inside the founder's answers is PROVISIONAL (delegate the overseer). The new read's answer is a like widening (the founder's fork), and it rests on a still-PROVISIONAL graph mark.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the cold-agent pipe's verbs take graph) — the pipe's `VERBS` hold thirteen words, and the fake server answers `graph` empty. It is uncounted, adding no verdict field or `capability-unused` reason. A new verb follows the same pattern in `scripts/cold-agent.sh` and `.github/scripts/test_cold_agent.py`.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the graph verb's command and tool_call lines) — the verb table went 12 → 13 and instance verbs 8 → 9. An accepted `graph` records `verb` alone and an argument is refused `malformed`. `host_log` / `mcp_log` each make one call at `trace` with `graph_needles` at 0, and `stand_mcp_tools` reads one `command` child. This is the direct precedent for every count and reading this chunk moves.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (dioxus-native-dom's graph modules and bridge dispatch add no log site) — `graph`, `signal_registry` and `stand_graph` are silent at a census reading of 0. The read reads these modules, so any reader it adds there joins this group's census.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the snapshot's clickable reading carries no page text) — `NodeState.clickable` is a closed bool (current listeners hold `click`, not a disabled control). This is one source of the read's actionable set, and it must stay text-free.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the state registry holds no state value) — `SignalRegistry` holds names, declarations and the dispatch chain, never a value, and its `Debug` prints counts alone. If the read draws handlers or owners from the graph's registry, its answer must keep this no-value line.

- per obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage (`command` span, fct-zuu6oxcq): any call reaching `Session::run` sits in the one hand-built INFO `command` span at target `escher_driver`, and that span keeps exactly its eight fields. A new read verb, if one is added, must record `verb` alone when accepted (no step run, as `snapshot`, `lint` and `graph` do) and `verb` + `cause` when refused. `verb` must be the verb table's own word, never the caller's text.
- per obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage (`tool_call` span): an MCP call of the new read must open one `tool_call` span holding only `tool` (the verb table's word) and `ending` (`accepted` · `refused` · `error`), with its `command` span as the child. No field may be added to either span.
- per obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage (never-fielded list): the read's answer must never be put in a span field. That covers its nodes, ids, owners, verb lists, per-verb refusal causes, its count or size, and any `Outcome`/`Command`/`Call`/`ArgValue`/`Refusal` (field or `Debug`). This matches the scope's span rule (fct-c7odudty).
- per obs-plan §3 Observability Harness Contract (Logging stack, fct-icom2cq7): escher-driver and every module the chunk touches or adds (schema, execute, json, describe, mcp, recording, replay) must install no subscriber, read no env var and print nothing. The new outcome must be written only by `Outcome::to_json`, as a command's answer, as the MCP JSON line, or kept whole in a recorded check. It must never be logged, fielded or printed with `Debug`.
- per obs-plan §6 Log Coverage (escher-driver emitter): the driver must add no event. The only lines in a sink-installing process stay the closed `command` and `tool_call` spans at `info` or below, with nothing at the default `warn`. escher-driver keeps its 2 `info_span!` sites.
- per obs-plan §8 PII Scrubbing & Compliance (fct-lhkfbl2j, the graph answer): the new read's answer may carry stable ids, verb names and closed cause words, like the `graph` answer that was ratified as a boundary widening. It must never carry a control's value or page text. Putting it on a carrier is a boundary widening, which is the founder's fork per the scope.
- per obs-plan §3 Observability Harness Contract (Logging stack): checks added for the read (the stand in both layout modes and the minimal fixtures for covered, off-screen and owner-served) must install no subscriber, read no env var and print nothing. Their readings go into assertions only, and the silence probe must read 0 over them and over the shared modules they read.

- The `graph` verb is the precedent per obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage: an accepted read records `verb` alone, and `stand_act_spans` drives one call of it per layout mode. `stand_mcp_tools` checks that the `tool_call` parents a `command` that records the verb alone.
- `host_log` and `mcp_log` each drive one `graph` call at `trace` and read 0 id, name and graph needles under both builds, per obs-plan §6 Log Coverage (fct-gwvelgmp). The same needle approach (ids, names, cause words) fits the new read.
- The cold-agent pipe's `VERBS` list holds the verb table's words (`graph` among them, uncounted, with no verdict field), per obs-plan §6 Log Coverage (fct-zygqqe4l). A new verb would follow it as an uncounted word, and its fake server would answer the new shape.

- No new span field, event, `#[instrument]` or log site for the read and its refusal pre-check. The shared refusal path (`action_point`) runs inside the call's `command` span and opens none of its own, per obs-plan §4 Span / Trace Coverage.

body:
Builds one read-only driver read of the current screen's actionable nodes (capability v030-06): per node its stable id, its optional owner element, its verbs, and per verb accepted-now or the one refusal cause a real call would return.
The node model is the UI graph's GraphNode with an optional owner; nothing is keyed on a DOM NodeId; the verbs are read from the schema's verb table VERBS with no closed list of verb names in this code, which may need VerbSpec to say more (a contract change, the founder's fork).
The refusal reasons come from the same path the executor uses (action_point: disabled, off-screen, covered), so the read agrees with a call by construction; it runs no step, dispatches nothing and changes nothing, like snapshot, lint and graph.
The actionable-key check (residual L12) may fold in as each node saying whether its id is an author key or a positional path, if it fits (a P4 question).
Proven on the stand in both layout modes, with minimal fixtures for a covered, an off-screen and an owner-served target where the stand lacks one.

body: The driver command schema: validate over the closed static verb table and bounded argument kinds, returning a typed Command or a Refusal; a new read, or a VerbSpec that says more, changes that table and must still pass every call through validate on the socket, the command line and MCP.

The typed Refusal: its closed set of causes with fixed names, meanings and remedies and no String field; the read names, per verb, only a cause the call would return (disabled, covered, off-screen), so no new free-text reason may appear.

The widening rule for the session socket and its carriers: a new field of a closed value set inside a ratified carrier is no widening, while a new carrier, a new exit, an open value set or authored text is; a new verb on every ratified carrier was a ratified widening for lint and graph, and this read's verb, carrier and answer shape are the founder's fork.

What the session socket's and MCP's bounded replies may carry: ids, names, closed flag words and booleans, a UI graph's ids, component, state and handler event names; never an attribute's text and never a NodeId; the read's answer carries ids, verb names and cause words only.

The stable element id: an author key when the HTML id is non-empty, slash-free and first, else an anchored, component or document path; the read reports these ids (and, with the L12 fold, which kind each is) and writes them to no log.

The command span rule: one command span per call recording verb and, refused, cause alone, fixed words, bools and counts only; no field holds the read's content or its size, and the crate installs no subscriber and reads no env var.
No unwrap, expect or panic on anything a call supplies, no clock read in the schema or validation, and no NodeId kept between calls, in the read's new code in escher-driver.

Recorded checks: a kept check's bytes read only through the strict Check::from_bytes with closed keys and schema-named arguments; a recorded step of the new read must fit that reader and still pass validate on replay, and the recording directory and file modes stay as they are.
The escher-session command line: the closed argv reader, validate before the session address is asked for, the four endings with fixed statuses, and no ending writing back anything the caller typed.
The MCP server's listing and results: bounded results, typed tool arguments through validate, fixed protocol errors with no data; the new read's tool joins under those bounds.
Masked values: a password's or file input's value stays MASKED_VALUE on every carrier; the read carries no control value, so it must not open a new path for one.

The UI graph and snapshot readers in dioxus-native-dom (graph handlers, snapshot clickable, unkeyed_actionable) and the in-process markup attribute readers for disabled and inert: read-only here unless P3 finds a reader missing, holding no log site or panic path on app input.
The engine-change rule: no engine change is expected; one that appears is the founder's fork, as a markup reader change for every document is a boundary widening.
Committed checks: only the two stand-Counter checks are committed; any check of a new fixture or session stays owner-only and is never committed.

body_fields.convention: each new escher-driver test or code path reads no env var but test-only build-time or TMPDIR sites registered as test-only, and names no secret
each new log line or span field holds fixed words, bools and counts only, never a call's content, screen text or a path, inside the escher_telemetry allowlist sink
each new fixture or test leaves no package entering Cargo.lock and builds under --locked
each new kept check or recorded fixture stays owner-only (0600 in a 0700 directory) and is never committed
each new test's panics on stale ids are guarded and code under test never panics on call-supplied input
